sessions.phase_label: Campaign outcome, relaunch planning, and indefinite hold

requirements.title: Twelve-Page Crowdfunding Sample Script
requirements.definition: Create the paid 12-page crowdfunding sample by adapting screenplay material into a professional page-and-panel comic script with appropriate dialogue, captions, visual direction, pacing, and presentation.
requirements.boundary_note: Page count, comic-script structure, pacing method, delivery timing, and permitted fidelity deviations are parameters of the same bounded sample deliverable. The later full-length script is separate because it has a distinct size, funding condition, and lifecycle.

requirements.title: Full Graphic Novel Script
requirements.definition: Create the prospective 80-85-page comic script for the first graphic novel as a separate post-crowdfunding production deliverable.
requirements.boundary_note: The page target, source-material choice, and narrative endpoint are attributes of one full-length adaptation deliverable. It remains separate from the paid sample because commencement depends on crowdfunding and it is independently deferred, reconsidered, and placed on hold.

unresolved_candidates.description: The 80-85-page target is clear, but the exact story coverage, preferred source material, and whether the volume should be self-contained or end with forward momentum remain unresolved attributes of the full-script Requirement.
The exchange may establish a standalone campaign-credit Requirement using the name Corodon Fuller, but the client does not explicitly confirm that the preferred credit will be used.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I would like to move forward with your 12-page sample. If you would like to accept please let me know and I will send the contract. The terms are as discussed in our messages. If you have any questions, please let me know. Otherwise, I will send it out shortly. Thanks!

value_updates.script_format: panel format for each comic page
value_updates.pacing_method: allocate panels and page space to individual story moments

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Here's an update: I've made some good progress today, and worked out a tentative breakdown that gets as far as Tom meeting Apollonia on comic page 12. I may end up deciding that pace is too brisk, if certain beats need more space to breathe--it's something I'll need to figure out as I go.
I have two questions, or rather two thoughts on how to approach the script that I want to check with you:
1.. In a few places I think I want to adapt parts of the scene descriptions into "voice over" caption text.
2\. There are a few short exchanges that I might want to omit for the sake of efficiency and page space. For example, at the bottom of page 23 where Carter tells Tom he's invited to the dinner he attends in the following scene.
I wanted to check whether deviations from the script of that size would be acceptable, or if you want the comic to represent the screenplay line-for-line. Let me know what you think.
Thanks.

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the sample must follow the screenplay line-for-line or may use voice-over captions and omit minor exchanges for pacing.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
In that case, thank you very much. For that rate I will be able to spend some more time on the best way to present everything, rather than relying so closely on the screenplay.

Would you like me to get started on this next week, or should I wait for you to say "go?"

I can commit to scripting 80-85 comic pages. I'll look over the next two episodes and the novel, and work out how much of the story to cover in that space. As I do that, should I pace things with an eye toward eventually scripting the rest of the story? That is, should I aim for something that feels self-contained, or focus on leaving the reader asking, "What's next?"

Thanks,
Cory
